newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on more profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on more profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended down for the second day in a row after another bout of profit-taking on Thursday, traders and analysts said.

"The market is now slightly overbought, and is going through a stabilization period which may be very short and pave the way for another rally," said Leonor Gonzalez, technical analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 13.87 points, or 0.41 percent, at 3,376.61. Volume was lacklustre at 62.3 million shares traded.
"The market was listless, and volume was thin. I think it's because the holiday season has begun," said a trader. "I feel a few foreign dealers may have been drawn back to the Dow Jones."
The Dow Jones ended up 14.16 points, or 0.22 percent, at 6.437.10. On the broad market, of 108 stocks traded, losers outnumbered winners by 57 to 19.
Financial stocks had a choppy day. Traders said the sector has been volatile due to speculation on the effects of applying international accountancy criteria to Mexican banks next year.
Financial stocks BBV Probursa and GFBital were first and fourth, respectively, on the gainers list, while another financial group, Serfin was a prominent loser.
Analysts were meanwhile cautiously optimistic the bourse was undergoing a consolidation period after a strong rally on Tuesday.
"If we can weaken the 3,450-point level at heavy volume, then we could reach 3,650 points by the end of December or early January," said Gonzalez.
